Risk B: The verifier might require that our reported `loads` sum matches flows exactly within 1e-5 including on failed edges. We compute from x. Good.

Risk C: The verifier constructs v with t=abs(x-a) and checks migration row sum t <= 2budget within 1e-5. Our x feasible for LP implies sum|x-a|<=2budget. Good. But wait, in the LP, the constraint is sum t_LP <= 2budget where t_LP >= |x-a|. Yes because each t_LP>=|x_j-a_j| by constraints (x-t<=a => t>=x-a; -x-t<=-a => t>=a-x; so t>=|x-a|). So sum|x-a|<=sum t_LP<=2budget. Good. So verifier's migration check passes.

Risk D: The verifier checks equality E v = d with v including t and U; E only involves x, so fine.

Risk E: The verifier's dual check: "Each dual column inequality has absolute tolerance 1e-7." It computes A^T y + E^T q <= c. For columns where our y from marginals might yield a tiny positive residual up to ~1e-16. Good.
